summary: Mendota (Bete Grise) Light, Keweenaw Peninsula: discontinued in 1870, rebuilt in 1895 as a brick tower, automated in 1933, privately owned and relit in 1998.

lens.where: restored fourth-order lens in the brick tower, in use since the 1998 relighting

light.characteristic: flashing white, one flash every 20 seconds (per the 1998 relighting accounts)

structures.note: USLHS: 36.66 ft from base to center of lantern; LighthouseFriends: just over 42 ft
Taken down by the tender Haze in 1871 and set up at Marquette Breakwater (1875, per LighthouseFriends)
The 1869 brick house was ruined by winter storms of 1893-94; replaced in 1895

access.note: Privately owned. LighthouseFriends: grounds, dwelling and tower closed. Michigan Tech archive: reachable only by boat. Owner's website describes a tour and weddings; ask the owner.

events.note: Congress appropriates $14,000 for a pierhead light to mark the Lac La Belle canal (2 March 1867)
Government takes a deed to a roughly two-acre site (9 May 1868)
Wooden pierhead tower and brick dwelling built under contract; completion 1869 per LighthouseFriends, November 1870 per the owner's history
Lit for about four and a half months under William Kirby
Discontinued after the 1870 navigation season
Wooden tower dismantled by the tender Haze and taken to Marquette Breakwater
Board asks for $7,500 to reestablish the light
Reestablishment authorized by act of 15 February 1893; no appropriation that year
Storms of the winter of 1893-94 ruin the old brick house; Board estimates $2,500 to replace the dwelling and recommends $10,000 instead of $7,500 for the reestablishment
New brick tower and dwelling built; appropriation of $7,500 made by the act of 2 March 1895
Fourth-order lens installed (USLHS: original lens installed 1895)
Fourth-order light established 30 November 1895
Changed from flashing to fixed white light, 31 October 1896
Keeper William G. Jilbert gives valuable assistance to three fishermen whose launch swamped near the station (28 April 1918)
Mendota keepers give food and shelter to shipwrecked sailors while the Eagle Harbor Coast Guard station assists two steamers (letter dated 31 December 1926)
Converted to electric incandescent
Unattended acetylene light on a square skeletal tower replaces the lighthouse
Decommissioned, per USLHS and Michigan Tech; Terry Pepper gives 1960
Harbor-of-refuge project dredges the canal and builds new piers at its entrance; the 1933 onshore tower is discontinued
Private residence until 1996; then offered for sale and sold to a buyer willing to conserve it (Michigan Tech). LighthouseFriends dates the Kohs purchase to 1998
Restored fourth-order lens; light relit by owner Gary Kohs on 5 July 1998 at 9:45 p.m.
Placed on the market in June 2020; sold 25 August 2020

corrections.why: The standing brick tower is the 1895 tower (USLHS: tower established 1895). The 1869 tower was a wooden pierhead tower, taken down in 1871 (LighthouseFriends), so the record's 1869 date and 'standing' status describe a structure that no longer exists.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The light was discontinued in 1870 and reestablished in 1895. It was automated in 1933 and decommissioned in 1956 (USLHS, Michigan Tech). A private owner relit it on 5 July 1998 and it is an active private aid to navigation (Michigan Tech).
The first light (wooden pierhead tower and brick dwelling, 1869) was lit in 1870 and discontinued the same year. The present tower dates from 1895 (USLHS tower date, Board reports).

notes_for_editor: Rich enough for a moderate story, not a full one: no newspaper coverage found (one Chronicling America search for 'Bete Grise' with lighthouse, 1895-1930, returned no pages); the NRHP nomination for 80004840 is not digitised (the file served is a placeholder image), so the 1980 listing date in the record is unverified here. The 1870 Board statement is quoted via LighthouseFriends (the 1870 report is not in the corpus); the 1892 Board report says the same thing in official words. Keichli/Kirby: the archive lists both for 1869-1870 while LighthouseFriends names only Kirby; not resolved. Completion date: LighthouseFriends 1869 vs owner's site November 1870. Appropriation: the 1894 report asked for $10,000 and the 1895 report records $7,500 by the act of 2 March 1895; the reports do not reconcile them. Relighting crowd: 3,500 (owner) vs roughly 1,000 (LighthouseFriends). Discontinuance year: 1956 (USLHS, Michigan Tech) vs 1960 (Terry Pepper). Sale year: Michigan Tech implies 1996, LighthouseFriends implies Kohs bought in 1998. Sale sequence, 1996-1998 (not resolved; the story says so): the Michigan Tech finding aid has the house offered for sale and sold to a conserving buyer in 1996; LighthouseFriends has Jaaskelainen buying at auction and keeping it until his death in 1996, with Kohs owner from 1998; the owner's history has the property sold at auction to Jaaskelainen and, after his death, bought by Kohs (no date given). Lamp lighter Nortdstrom is listed from 1939, after the 1933 automation date; no source here says what the post was. Journals (1895-1930) are at Michigan Tech and not transcribed. The current owner (sold 2020) is deliberately not named: he is a private individual and the owner's own page does not give his name in print. Kohs and Jaaskelainen are named only in their public role as restorer and buyer. Height: 36.66 ft to lantern (USLHS) vs just over 42 ft (LighthouseFriends). The record's light characteristic (Fl W 20s) and focal height were not re-verified against the Light List. Visit status: USLHS lists the station as open to the public; LighthouseFriends says grounds closed; the owner's site advertises tours. Coordinates in the record (47.374, -87.967) and USLHS (47.3731, -87.9572) differ slightly; not treated as a correction. Quotes from LighthouseFriends and the owner's website are used only to verify facts; the published prose paraphrases them.
